title: Effective pruning of task-trained recurrent neural networks using noisy fluctuations and connection rescaling
abstract: arXiv:2608.05464v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Pruning network connections is key to brain function but, despite its importance, there exist few biologically-plausible pruning rules with demonstrated good performance. We evaluate noise-prune, a recently introduced unsupervised local pruning rule for recurrent networks that uses noisy fluctuations to determine the importance of connections. Noise-prune has previously only been empirically tested on random networks without a specific computational function. We show that noise-prune preserves task-performance in task-trained recurrent neural networks, greatly outperforming a strategy that only uses connection magnitude and exceeding a non-local strategy that uses second-order information. Rather than deterministically removing connections that fall below a threshold, noise-prune samples connections to preserve based on their importance and strengthens retained connections to preserve average strength. translated_title: 利用噪声波动与连接重缩放对任务训练的循环神经网络进行有效剪枝
translated_abstract: 剪枝（删除）网络连接对大脑功能至关重要，但尽管其重要性，目前具有良好性能且符合生物学合理性的剪枝规则却很少。我们评估了noise-prune——一种近期提出的用于循环网络的无监督局部剪枝规则，它利用噪声波动来确定连接的重要性。此前noise-prune仅在无特定计算功能的随机网络上进行过经验性测试。我们证明，noise-prune能够在任务训练的循环神经网络中保持任务性能，大幅优于仅依据连接权重大小的策略，并超过了使用二阶信息的非局部策略。与确定性地删除低于阈值的连接不同，noise-prune根据重要性对要保留的连接进行随机采样，并加强被保留的连接以维持平均连接强度。我们进一步证明，这种采样机制……
tldr: 该研究将noise-prune剪枝规则成功应用于任务训练的循环神经网络，通过基于噪声波动对连接重要性进行采样并重缩放保留连接的强度来保持任务性能，其效果优于基于权重大小和二阶信息的剪枝策略。
en_tdlr: This study shows that noise-prune—an unsupervised local pruning rule that samples connections by noisy fluctuations and rescales retained connections—effectively prunes task-trained recurrent neural networks while preserving task performance, outperforming magnitude-based and second-order pruning strategies.
